63938-medicine-in-the-middle-ages-extrac.creator: Unknown
63938-medicine-in-the-middle-ages-extrac.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. aron, Rhazes, Haly-Abas, Avicenna, Avenzoar, Averrhoes, Albucasis, and other writers, who continued the work left by the Greeks, leaving remarkable books on medicine and surgery. Unfortunately the ordinance of Islamism prevented these scientists from following anatomical work too closely, and consequently limited the progress they might otherwise have made in medicine.[1]

arxiv-2202-02061.title: Monoidal Streams for Dataflow Programming
arxiv-2202-02061.creator: Elena Di Lavore, Giovanni de Felice, Mario Román
arxiv-2202-02061.description: Abstract . We introduce monoidal streams: a generalization of causal stream functions to monoidal categories. They have a feedback structure that gives semantics to signal flow graphs. In the same way that streams provide semantics to dataflow programming with pure functions, monoidal streams provide semantics to dataflow programming with theories of processes represented by a symmetric monoidal category.

arxiv-2305-12592.title: Scattering off a junction
arxiv-2305-12592.creator: Eric Tan, R. Ganesh
arxiv-2305-12592.description: Abstract Scattering off a potential is a fundamental problem in quantum physics. It has been studied extensively with amplitudes derived for various potentials. In this article, we explore a setting with no potentials, where scattering occurs off a junction where many wires meet.

arxiv-2308-13059.title: Complex motion of steerable vesicular robots filled with active colloidal rods
arxiv-2308-13059.creator: Sophie Y. Lee, Philipp W. A. Schönhöfer, Sharon C. Glotzer
arxiv-2308-13059.description: Abstract While the collective motion of active particles has been studied extensively, effective strategies to navigate particle swarms without external guidance remain elusive. We introduce a method to control the trajectories of two-dimensional swarms of active rod-like particles by confining the particles to rigid bounding membranes (vesicles) with non-uniform curvature.

arxiv-2401-08927.title: Comment on arXiv:2312.04495 by M. I. Eremets and coauthors
arxiv-2401-08927.creator: J. E. Hirsch
arxiv-2401-08927.description: Abstract In the recently posted arXiv:2312.04495v3 talv3 , its authors used a computer code written by me supplied to them by the authors of Ref. hmtrapped , and claimed that the results that they obtained invalidate the results and conclusions presented in the paper J. Supercond. Nov. Mag. 35, 3141-3145 (2022) by F. Marsiglio and myself hmtrapped .

arxiv-2402-04818.title: An advanced scheme for queue management in TCP/IP networks
arxiv-2402-04818.creator: Abderrahmane Boudi 1 , Malik Loudini 1
arxiv-2402-04818.description: Abstract Active Queue Management (AQM) is a key congestion control scheme that aims to find a balance between keeping high link utilization, minimizing queuing delays, and ensuring a fair share of the bandwidth between the competing flows. Traditional AQM mechanisms use only information that is present at the intermediate nodes (routers).

arxiv-2402-09804.title: Coevolution of relationship and interaction in cooperative dynamical multiplex networks
arxiv-2402-09804.creator: Xiaojin Xiong, Ziyan Zeng, Minyu Feng, Attila Szolnoki
arxiv-2402-09804.description: Abstract While actors in a population can interact with anyone else freely, social relations significantly influence our inclination towards particular individuals. The consequence of such interactions, however, may also form the intensity of our relations established earlier. These dynamical processes are captured via a coevolutionary model staged in multiplex networks with two distinct layers.

arxiv-2403-03928.title: Pattern preserving quasi-isometries in lamplighter groups and other related groups
arxiv-2403-03928.creator: Tullia Dymarz, Beibei Liu, Nataša Macura, Rose Morris-Wright
arxiv-2403-03928.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Tullia Dymarz, Beibei Liu, Nataša Macura, Rose Morris-Wright. In this paper we explore the interplay between aspects of the geometry and algebra of three families of groups of the form B ⋊ ℤ B\rtimes{\mathbb{Z}} , namely Lamplighter groups, solvable Baumslag-Solitar groups and lattices in SOL. In particular we examine what kind of maps are induced on B B by quasi-isometries that coarsely permute cosets of the ℤ {\mathbb{Z}} subgroup.

arxiv-2404-00935.title: Random Circuit Sampling: Fourier Expansion and Statistics
arxiv-2404-00935.creator: Gil Kalai, Yosef Rinott, Tomer Shoham
arxiv-2404-00935.description: Abstract Considerable effort in experimental quantum computing is devoted to noisy intermediate scale quantum computers (NISQ computers). Understanding the effect of noise is important for various aspects of this endeavor including notable claims for achieving quantum supremacy and attempts to demonstrate quantum error correcting codes.

arxiv-2407-16382.title: TookaBERT: A Step Forward for Persian NLU
arxiv-2407-16382.creator: MohammadAli SadraeiJavaheri, Ali Moghaddaszadeh, Milad Molazadeh, Fariba Naeiji
arxiv-2407-16382.description: Abstract The field of natural language processing (NLP) has seen remarkable advancements, thanks to the power of deep learning and foundation models. Language models, and specifically BERT, have been key players in this progress. In this study, we trained and introduced two new BERT models using Persian data.

arxiv-2407-21681.title: Homogeneous Magnetic Flux in Rydberg Lattices
arxiv-2407-21681.creator: J. Eix +, R. Bai +, T. Lahaye, A. Browaeys, H. P. Büchler, S. Weber
arxiv-2407-21681.description: Abstract We present a method for generating homogeneous and tunable magnetic flux for bosonic particles in a lattice using Rydberg atoms. Our setup relies on Rydberg excitations hopping through the lattice by dipolar exchange interactions. The magnetic flux arises from complex hopping via ancilla atoms.

arxiv-2411-14495.title: Test-Time Adaptation of 3D Point Clouds via Denoising Diffusion Models
arxiv-2411-14495.creator: Hamidreza Dastmalchi, Aijun An, Ali Cheraghian, Shafin Rahman, Sameera Ramasinghe
arxiv-2411-14495.description: Abstract Test-time adaptation (TTA) of 3D point clouds is crucial for mitigating discrepancies between training and testing samples in real-world scenarios, particularly when handling corrupted point clouds. LiDAR data, for instance, can be affected by sensor failures or environmental factors, causing domain gaps. Adapting models to these distribution shifts online is crucial, as training for every possible variation is impractical.

arxiv-2502-02949.title: The physics of oscillating surfaces and sounds
arxiv-2502-02949.creator: Md Hossen Mondal, Ramkrishna Joshi
arxiv-2502-02949.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Md Hossen Mondal, Ramkrishna Joshi. The longitudinal oscillations of air columns composed of contractions and rarefactions make up sound. Sound amplification is widely used in medical, electronic and communication fields. A simplistic technique for producing and amplifying can be rewarding. In this study, we investigate a simplistic DIY speaker configuration that can be utilized for sound creation and modulation by implementing response of magnets and a solenoid to an oscillating input signal.

arxiv-2506-02295.title: QARI-OCR: High-Fidelity Arabic Text Recognition through Multimodal Large Language Model Adaptation
arxiv-2506-02295.creator: Ahmed Wasfy, Omer Nacar, Abdelakreem Elkhateb, Mahmoud Reda, Omar Elshehy, Adel Ammar, Wadii Boulila
arxiv-2506-02295.description: Abstract The inherent complexities of Arabic script—its cursive nature, diacritical marks (tashkeel), and varied typography—pose persistent challenges for Optical Character Recognition (OCR). We present Qari-OCR, a series of vision-language models derived from Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct, progressively optimized for Arabic through iterative fine-tuning on specialized synthetic datasets. Our leading model, QARI v0.

arxiv-2512-04948.creator: Arkady A. Tseytlin and Zihan Wang
arxiv-2512-04948.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Arkady A. Tseytlin and Zihan Wang. We review and elaborate on the issue of 3d world volume supersymmetry that appears as a residual part of global target space supersymmetry in the BST supermembrane action.

arxiv-2601-15804.title: Entangled Life and Code: A Computational Design Taxonomy for Synergistic Bio-Digital Systems Conference: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems; April 13–17, 2026; Barcelona, Spain Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI
arxiv-2601-15804.creator: Zoë Breed, Elvin Karana, Alessandro Bozzon, Katherine W. Song
arxiv-2601-15804.description: Abstract . Bio-digital systems that merge microbial life with technology promise new modes of computation, combining biological adaptability with digital precision. Yet realizing this potential symbiotically – where biological and digital agents co-adapt and co-process – remains elusive, largely due to the absence of a shared vocabulary bridging biology and computing.

pmc-10620333.creator: Beomjun Kim, In-Hwan Oh, Hyeon-Kyoung Cheong, Jun-Won Hwang
pmc-10620333.description: Objective We aimed to investigate the annual prevalence of intellectual disabilities (ID) and autism spectrum disorder employing claims data registered in Korean National Health Insurance Service. We also estimated the annual average of medical costs incurred from these disorders using same datasets.

pmc-11396666.title: Time-Resolved Circular Dichroism in Molecules: Experimental and Theoretical Advances
pmc-11396666.creator: Marta Monti, Leonardo Biancorosso, Emanuele Coccia
pmc-11396666.description: Following changes in chirality can give access to relevant information on the function or reactivity of molecular systems. Time-resolved circular dichroism (TRCD) spectroscopy proves to be a valid tool to achieve this goal. Depending on the class of molecules, different temporal ranges, spanning from seconds to femtoseconds, need to be investigated to observe such chiroptical changes.

pmc-11541479.title: Phase-separated chromatin compartments: Orchestrating gene expression through condensation
pmc-11541479.creator: Xin Li, Chengzhi Liu, Zhichao Lei, Huan Chen, Liang Wang
pmc-11541479.description: Eukaryotic genomes are organized into distinct chromatin compartments, some of which exhibit properties of biomolecular condensates. These condensates primarily form due to chromatin-associated proteins/complexes (CAPs). CAPs play a crucial role in gene expression, functioning as either transcriptional repressors or activators. Phase separation, a well-established biophysical phenomenon, is a key driver of chromatin condensate formation by CAPs.

pmc-11677215.title: A Seed Endophytic Bacterium Cronobacter dublinensis BC-14 Enhances the Growth and Drought Tolerance of Echinochloa crus-galli
pmc-11677215.creator: Sheng Cheng, Qingling Wang, Dashan Yang, Quanlong He, Jianxin Deng, Yi Zhou, Lin Zhang, Jianwei Jiang, Gary A Strobel
pmc-11677215.description: Successful seed germination and plant seedling growth often require association with endophytic bacteria. Barnyard grass (Echinochloa crus-galli (L.) P. Beauv.) is a main weed during rice cultivation and has frequently been found in drought-prone fields such as cornfields in recent years.

pmc-11683263.title: Always Prioritise Your Priorities, Especially During Pandemics
pmc-11683263.creator: María P Lamarca Mendoza
pmc-11683263.description: ar procedures.1 The study cohort consisted of 3 150 patients who were prospectively collected from 20 March – 31 August 2020. It revealed that most deaths were in hospital (9.1%), with a 30 day mortality rate of 10.4% and a six month mortality rate of 12.8%, which is significantly higher than pre-pandemic published data.

pmc-11732321.title: Use of ceramic synthetic allografts in spine surgery: a narrative review with early basic science and clinic data of novel nanosynthetic bone graft
pmc-11732321.creator: Christopher L Antonacci, Annabelle P Davey, Cameron Kia, Hanbing Zhou
pmc-11732321.description: Background and ObjectiveAs the global population ages, degenerative spinal disorders are on the rise, leading to an increased focus on optimizing spinal fusion therapies. Despite the high success rate of iliac crest bone autografts, their usage is hampered by donor site morbidity and limited supply.

pmc-12535080.title: Global burden and cross-country inequalities in head and neck cancer from 1992 to 2021: results from the global burden of disease study
pmc-12535080.creator: Shijie Sun, Manman Lu, Shen’ao Wei, Yuwei Liang, Ziyi Zhang, Huadong Wang, Lei Si
pmc-12535080.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundHead and neck cancer (HNC) caused substantial morbidity and mortality. Despite advances in treatment modalities, the evolving burden and risk factor profiles of head and neck cancer may contribute to escalating health inequalities.

pmc-12539871.title: Detección de los errores innatos del metabolismo: directrices en México y otros países
pmc-12539871.creator: Sarahi Guerrero-Barrios, Mariana Chiquillo-Domínguez, Jorge Ayón-Aguilar, Sergio Elihu Rodriguez-Alfaro, Socorro Méndez-Martínez, Máximo Alejandro García-Flores
pmc-12539871.description: ResumenLos errores innatos del metabolismo (EIM), también conocidos como trastornos metabólicos hereditarios, son poco comunes, pero se asocian con importante morbilidad y mortalidad. La incidencia es variable en todas las regiones, a nivel mundial oscila de 1 entre 569 a 2500 recién nacidos vivos (RNV).

pmc-12785957.title: Inflammatory Co-Regulation of Voltage-Gated Sodium Channels and Na,K-ATPase in Metastatic Breast Cancer
pmc-12785957.creator: Steven D. Scahill, Kelly Jean Sherman, Dennis Paul
pmc-12785957.description: Sodium regulation is a potentially major driver of cancer metastasis. Voltage-gated sodium channels (VGSCs) and Na,K-ATPase are sodium transporters that are upregulated in many advanced carcinomas and are implicated as metastatic drivers. However, little is known about what drives this overexpression, how these proteins influence metastatic behavior, or whether these complementary sodium transporters are co-regulated in cancer.

pmc-13031796.title: Synergistic dye removal through curcumin functionalized MCM-22 zeolite as a photocatalyst nanocomposite via the simultaneous photocatalysis and adsorption method
pmc-13031796.creator: Elaheh Shadi, Mehdi Amirinejad, Ali Ashraf Derakhshan, Hooman Rezaie
pmc-13031796.description: This paper investigates the efficiency of simultaneous adsorption/photocatalyst system for dye removal. A novel composite material consisting of curcumin functionalized MCM-22 zeolite, titanium dioxide (TiO₂) and cerium nanoparticles was utilized. TiO₂ nanoparticles were layered by reacting zeolite with a titanium butoxide solution, followed by cerium incorporation using cerium nitrate.

pmc-13172963.title: 129 From plate to pillow: The effects of ultra-processed foods (UPFs) on sleep duration and memory in adults over 60 years of age
pmc-13172963.creator: Valerie Marshall, Junxin Li
pmc-13172963.description: Objectives/Goals: The objective of my study is to examine the relationship between ultra-processed foods, sleep duration, and memory in adults aged 60 years and older. Diet and sleep are often studied independently as modifiable risk factors for cognitive decline; a growing body of evidence suggests a unique nexus between the two with regard to cognitive outcomes.

pmc-13411695.title: Lithium Chloride-Induced Nuclear Envelope Remodeling in 3D Endometrial Cancer Spheroids
pmc-13411695.creator: Ayhan Bilir, Berna Yıldırım, Mete Hakan Karalök, Kudret Kulak
pmc-13411695.description: Selective remodeling of nuclear architecture under pharmacological stress remains incompletely characterized in three-dimensional cancer models, particularly at the ultrastructural level. Lithium chloride (LiCl) is widely used as a cellular stressor capable of altering membrane organization, proliferation, and organelle dynamics; however, its effects on nucleus-associated structural remodeling in three-dimensional tumor systems remain unclear.

pmc-13533843.title: Health effects associated with alcohol consumption: a Burden of Proof study
pmc-13533843.creator: Xiaochen Dai, Sneha I. Nicholson, Hilary R. Lawlor, Sinclair Carr, Jaimie D. Steinmetz, Natalie M. Chen, Susan A. McLaughlin, Simon I. Hay, Kanyin L. Ong, Aleksandr Y. Aravkin, Peng Zheng, Reed J. D. Sorensen, Nora M. Gilbertson, Erin C. Mullany, Erin M. O’Connell, Christopher J. L. Murray, Emmanuel
pmc-13533843.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The relationship between alcohol and health is complex, and the evidence relating alcohol consumption to various cardiovascular diseases, cancers and other conditions is evolving. Moreover, alcohol drinking guidelines vary widely. Here we conducted 16 systematic reviews across four databases and conservatively re-evaluated dose–response relationships between alcohol consumption and 20 health outcomes, analysing 843 cohort and case–control studies using the Burden of Proof meta-analytic framework.

pmc-13577465.title: PSAFM: A parameter-free spatial attention fusion module
pmc-13577465.creator: Guangjun Liu, Xiaoping Xu, Bingkun Zhou, Feng Wang, Yike Li
pmc-13577465.description: Attention mechanisms improve convolutional neural networks (CNNs) by emphasizing informative features, but many existing modules introduce additional parameters, convolutional or fully connected layers, and non-negligible computational overhead. These costs may limit their use in lightweight or plug-and-play CNN architectures. To address this issue, this paper proposes a parameter-free spatial attention fusion module (PSAFM).

pmc-13648358.title: The engagement of layer 6 corticothalamic neurons in somatosensation
pmc-13648358.creator: Elaida D Dimwamwa, Nelson H Chang, Christian Waiblinger, Garrett B Stanley
pmc-13648358.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The corticothalamic neurons from layer 6 (L6CT) of primary sensory cortices provide extensive input to the thalamus in addition to projecting across layers intracortically, positioning them to play a key hypothesized role in shaping thalamocortical signaling. With the expansion of tools for precise functional identification of L6CT neurons during in-vivo electrophysiology, increasing evidence highlights L6CT neurons as dynamic gain modulators of thalamocortical sensory responses.
